answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a sponsored insurance market: a newcomer earns only after an unrelated established agent posts a bond on its behalf, like a pigment bond that stains the sponsor if the newcomer cheats. Sponsors investigate first, because a proven fake forfeits their bond, while honest newcomers earn the sponsor a fee. One operator wanting a thousand fakes must find a thousand sponsors risking money on each, and the ripple of one exposed fake scares off future sponsors, so the spiral of cost grows faster than any fake profit, while a genuine agent needs just one sponsor.
